title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: KEISHA'S LOT
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Keisha, a night-shift grocery worker in Tulsa, Oklahoma.
Across from her house sat an empty lot. Weeds, old tires, and one very sad couch.
Keisha decided to turn it into a garden.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE BINDER
segments.author: Henry David Thoreau
lines: First, she made a big plan. A fountain, a chicken coop, and lights on every fence post.
The binder was three inches thick. She had not dug one hole.
On her break, she opened an old copy of Walden by Henry David Thoreau, and read two words:
Simplify, simplify.
So she closed the binder. One bed. Tomatoes. Start there.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE TIRES
segments.quote: Put your shoulder to the wheel.
segments.author: Aesop
lines: But first, the lot had to be cleaned. She called the city three times. Nobody came.
Her grandma used to tell an Aesop fable about a man waiting for help with his stuck wagon. The lesson:
Put your shoulder to the wheel.
So Keisha rented a truck, and hauled out twenty-three tires and the sad couch herself.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE DIRT
segments.quote: Adopt the pace of nature: her secret is patience.
segments.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
lines: She planted the seeds. Every morning after her shift, she stared at the dirt. Two weeks. Nothing.
Old Mr. Ortiz from next door laughed from his porch, and quoted the writer Ralph Waldo Emerson:
Adopt the pace of nature: her secret is patience.
So she stopped staring, and started watering. Three days later, green.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE HAIL
segments.quote: It ain't over till it's over.
segments.author: Yogi Berra
lines: Then, in July, a hailstorm flattened every plant in ten minutes.
Keisha sat in the mud, ready to quit.
Her brother Marcus, a lifelong baseball fan, texted her the words of Yankees catcher Yogi Berra:
It ain't over till it's over.
The next Saturday, Marcus showed up with seeds, two shovels, and donuts.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE OKRA
segments.quote: It is a bad plan that admits of no modification.
segments.author: Publilius Syrus
lines: But the new tomatoes cooked in the Oklahoma heat. A hundred and two degrees.
Mr. Ortiz shook his head, and quoted an old Roman writer, Publilius Syrus:
It is a bad plan that admits of no modification.
So she switched to okra and peppers, plants that love the heat. They grew like crazy.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE SIGN
segments.quote: When you can do the common things of life in an uncommon way, you will command the attention of the world.
segments.author: George Washington Carver
lines: Now she had too much okra. So she gave it away, with a handwritten recipe in every bag.
On the gate, she painted words from the plant scientist George Washington Carver:
When you can do the common things of life in an uncommon way, you will command the attention of the world.
Today, fourteen neighbors grow food in that lot. Mr. Ortiz grows the best peppers in Tulsa.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Keep it simple. Do the work. Be patient. Don't quit. Change the plan. Do it your way.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Keep it simple. Do the work yourself. Be patient. Don't quit. Change the plan. And do ordinary things your own way.
As for me, my garden only grows one thing. Excuses.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
